research_problem: Code LLMs hallucinate invocations of low-frequency (new, updated, rare) APIs; naive documentation retrieval can hurt well-known APIs
technical_approach: CloudAPIBench: 622 synthetic Python tasks invoking AWS/Azure SDK APIs with The Stack v2 frequency labels (low/medium/high); validity via binding to documentation-derived API stubs; iterative Documentation Augmented Generation (BM25, configurable-precision retriever) with augmentation-design ablations; selective retrieval via API-index lookup and API-name token confidence (DAG++)
primary_contribution: Frequency-stratified API hallucination benchmark and evidence-based selective documentation retrieval
dataset_benchmark: CloudAPIBench (622 tasks, AWS and Azure); StarCoder2, CodeGemma, Granite-Code, GPT-4o
evaluation_metrics: Valid API invocation rate by frequency group, retrieval trigger rate, tokens per augmentation
baselines: Base models without retrieval; DAG always-retrieve; index lookup; confidence gating
key_findings: All models hallucinate, strongly correlated with API frequency (GPT-4o 38.58% valid on low-frequency APIs); API specification is the key documentation element (41.80% -> 86.82%); high-frequency APIs need >80% retriever precision (50% precision drops 84.39% -> 67.32%); DAG costs GPT-4o 39.02 points on high-frequency APIs; confidence is well calibrated; DAG++ retrieves 3.41% for high vs 50.56% for low frequency and adds 8.20 points for GPT-4o
author_limitations: Python-only short synthetic prompts; heuristic construction and frequency estimation; iterative latency; generated code needs review/sandboxing
analyst_limitations: Stub binding checks signatures not argument values, API choice semantics or execution; simulated retriever precision; synthetic LLM-written prompts; name-based frequency counts; ablations on one small model without variance; release status unclear; SDK rather than raw REST/OpenAPI
reproducibility: Medium: open models; benchmark availability uncertain; dated GPT-4o snapshot
suggested_extensions: Confidence-gated OpenAPI/MCP operation retrieval for agents; execution-validated hallucination benchmarks; longitudinal hallucination after API releases; effect of documentation quality on DAG; security-relevant API hallucination
evidence_location: Benchmark p.3; results p.4 Table 1; DAG ablations p.5-6; selective retrieval p.6-8 Tables 2-3; limitations p.9
integrity: Column interleaving lost some abstract text and headings; tables column-split; figures missing; appendix unread
